title: Choosing the Right Structure
description: Apply a decision framework to select the best data structure for access patterns, mutation frequency, and memory constraints.

data.text: No single data structure wins in every scenario. Arrays offer fast random access, linked lists offer cheap insertions, hash tables offer near-constant lookups, and trees offer hierarchical organization. The skill is matching the structure to the problem's dominant operations.
Start by asking three questions: What is the most frequent operation? Is the dataset static or changing? How much memory is acceptable? The answers narrow the field quickly.

data.title: Steps to choose a structure
items: List the operations you perform most: lookup, insert, delete, or iterate.
Note whether you need ordering, uniqueness, or key-based access.
Estimate the data size and growth rate.
Pick the simplest structure that meets the performance target.

rows: Great for ordered data with range queries

data.title: Choosing for a session cache
data.content: A web app needs to cache user sessions by ID and expire old sessions when memory is tight.

data.text: In the session cache example, the dominant operation is lookup by ID, which points directly to a hash table. The secondary concern is eviction policy, which is often handled with a secondary structure such as a linked list.

data.title: Common trade-offs
items: Speed vs memory: hash tables use more memory for buckets.
Ordering vs simplicity: trees preserve order but add pointer overhead.
Cache locality vs flexibility: arrays cache well; linked lists do not.
Simplicity vs optimization: premature optimization can add complexity without measurable gain.

data.title: Start simple
data.text: Choose the simplest structure that meets your performance target. An array is often the right answer. Move to more complex structures only when profiling or reasoning shows the need.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Identify your dominant operation before choosing a structure.
Use comparison tables to narrow candidates quickly.
Accept trade-offs consciously rather than chasing perfection.
data.takeaway: Choosing the right structure is a design skill that improves with deliberate practice and real-world benchmarking.
